topic: What if you could switch off sleep?
part: Chapter 2 of 6: the fun part, night one (long-form, ~50 s)
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SWITCH OFF SLEEP?
previous_text: One flip, and you never feel tired again. Not once. Not ever.

script.text: Normally, you'd lose the next eight hours. Tonight, they're yours.
You read the book you've ignored since summer. Then the next one. Then the whole shelf.
Eight hours a night is two thousand nine hundred twenty hours a year. Four extra months. Every year. That's real.
You finish every assignment. Even the ones that haven't been assigned yet.
You watch a whole season of a show in one night. Then you text your friends about it. Nobody answers. They're asleep. Losers.
By sunrise, you've done a week of homework, read six books, and you feel… great. No coffee. No yawning. Nothing.

science.claim: Eight hours a night is 2,920 hours a year, about four months
science.source: arithmetic; assumes 8 h of sleep a night (the CDC recommends 7+ h for adults, 8-10 h for teens 13-18)
